message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the most recent common ancestor of the clade that contains both families—Felidae (cats) and Equidae (horses, zebras, etc.). In other words, it is the last common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** (to which lions belong) and **Perissodactyla** (to which zebras belong). This ancestor lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, in the late Cretaceous period, before the divergence of the major lineages that eventually gave rise to modern cats and horses.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. We need to answer. There's no tool needed. Just provide an answer. The question is about biology: lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). They belong to different families: lions are Felidae, zebras are Equidae. Both are mammals, order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla. The common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Or maybe the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both families. That might be the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. But the question likely expects something like "the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which lived around 70 million years ago." Or maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the mammalian clade that includes both families, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals. But we can give a more precise answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla. This ancestor lived approximately 70-80 million years ago during the late Cretaceous period.

We can mention that the last common ancestor of all placental mammals is older (~100-120 million years ago). But the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families Felidae and Equidae. So we can say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, dating back to the late Cretaceous period (~70-80 million years ago).

Thus answer accordingly.
